questions.explain: Standard RIs give the maximum discount but the instance family is fixed (db.r6i can't cover db.r7g); Convertible RIs take a somewhat smaller discount but can be exchanged for different instance types, regions, or engines — valuable within 18–24 months of an architecture change.

questions.explain: Regional RIs apply to any matching instance in any AZ in the region with AZ flexibility; Zonal RIs apply to one AZ and guarantee capacity there — Regional is almost always correct for production databases.
options: Regional RIs apply to any matching instance in any AZ within the region (AZ flexibility); Zonal RIs apply to a specific AZ and guarantee capacity there

Scope only affects payment terms, not capacity behavior

questions.explain: Azure reserves at the vCore level and a reservation floats across databases as they scale; the Hybrid Benefit can stack on top with SA licenses. And Azure RI discounts apply to compute only — storage is separate and not discountable.

They discount compute and storage together
They require a matching reservation per database with no vCore pooling

questions.explain: Commit at the P75 utilization level for stable workloads (headroom for P95 spikes stays on-demand); seasonal workloads commit at base load and let bursts run on-demand — sized from at least 90 days of utilization data, not current provisioning.
